issues.legal_issue: A tenancy created by a mortgagee in possession ordinarily ends when the mortgagee’s interest ends, unless the mortgagor or successor adopts or recreates the tenancy, or the lease binds as a prudent act of management.
material_facts: A mortgagee in possession leased an urban cinema property to a head lessee, who sublet it.
The lease imposed a low rent and provided for a lengthy term, including renewals; the property could have obtained a substantially higher rent.
The property was sold to satisfy the mortgage debt, extinguishing the mortgagee’s interest, and the purchaser did not adopt or recreate the tenancies.
The mortgagor had cancelled an earlier rent note and permitted the mortgagees to lease the property, but had not expressly agreed to a tenancy continuing beyond the mortgage.
issues.conclusion: The tenancies did not bind the purchaser after the mortgagee’s interest ended. The purchaser was entitled to possession before the stated lease term and renewals expired.
issues.legal_principle: A person cannot confer a better title than that person holds. A mortgagee’s interest as lessor is ordinarily coterminous with the mortgage interest, and under section 111(c) of the Transfer of Property Act a lease determines when the lessor’s interest terminates. Under section 76(a), a mortgagee in possession must manage the property as a person of ordinary prudence would manage it; a bona fide and prudent act in the ordinary course of management may bind successors after the mortgage ends. That exception did not apply to this long, low-rent lease. The Court relied on Mahabir Gope v. Harbans Narain Singh, [1952] S.C.R. 775, and Asaram v. Mst. Ram Kali, [1958] S.C.R. 986.

rule.if: possession_suit_after_mortgage_interest_ended and mortgagee_created_tenancy and successor_did_not_adopt_tenancy and (lease_not_prudent_management or no_express_post_mortgage_consent)

predicates.possession_suit_after_mortgage_interest_: A person claiming through ownership sought possession after the mortgage interest had ended.
predicates.mortgagee_created_tenancy: A mortgagee in possession created a tenancy over the mortgaged property.
predicates.successor_did_not_adopt_tenancy: The person succeeding to the mortgagor’s interest did not adopt or recreate the tenancy.
predicates.lease_not_prudent_management: The mortgagee granted a lease on terms that were not a prudent act of ordinary property management.
predicates.no_express_post_mortgage_consent: The mortgagor did not expressly agree that the tenancy would continue beyond the mortgage.

issues.definition: When a possession claim follows the end of a mortgage interest, a tenancy created by the mortgagee ends with that interest if the successor did not adopt it and it was neither prudent management nor expressly agreed to continue.

issues.legal_issue: Rent-restriction protection does not continue for a tenancy that ends when the mortgagee’s interest is extinguished.
material_facts: The subtenants claimed protection under the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949.
Under the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951, the property was sold to satisfy the mortgage debt, and the sale extinguished the mortgagee’s interest.
The purchaser acquired full title, and no tenancy survived or was recreated after the mortgage ended.
issues.conclusion: The Rent Restriction Act did not protect the subtenants after the mortgagee’s interest ended because no landlord-and-tenant relationship remained.
issues.legal_principle: The Rent Restriction Act’s definitions of landlord and tenant apply only where a real or statutory tenancy survives. Section 10 of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 permitted the competent officer to use measures including sale of the mortgaged property to satisfy the mortgage debt. Here the sale satisfied the mortgage and extinguished the mortgagee’s interest, leaving no continuing landlord-and-tenant relationship to which rent-restriction protection could attach.

rule.if: rent_protection_claimed and mortgage_property_sold_to_satisfy_debt and mortgage_interest_extinguished and no_surviving_tenancy

predicates.rent_protection_claimed: A tenant or subtenant claimed protection under a rent-restriction regime.
predicates.mortgage_property_sold_to_satisfy_debt: The mortgaged property was sold to satisfy the mortgage debt.
predicates.mortgage_interest_extinguished: The transaction extinguished the mortgagee’s interest in the property.
predicates.no_surviving_tenancy: No real or statutory tenancy survived, and no new tenancy was created.

issues.definition: A rent-protection claim does not succeed when the property is sold to satisfy the mortgage, the mortgage interest is extinguished, and no tenancy survives.

issues.legal_issue: Mesne profits may be limited to the actual rent on which the premises were held when the evidence does not justify a higher award.
material_facts: The purchaser sought mesne profits from the occupants after seeking possession.
The premises had been held at an actual rent, although there was uncertainty about whether that rent included the use of a passage.
The lower court had reduced the claimed mesne profits to the actual rent, and the Supreme Court considered that figure low but found no basis to disturb it.
issues.conclusion: The award of mesne profits at the actual rent was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the amount fixed by the High Court because it reflected the actual rent on which the premises were held, notwithstanding that it was low and there was some uncertainty about what the rent included.

predicates.mesne_profits_appeal: An appeal challenged the amount awarded as mesne profits for occupied premises.
predicates.actual_rent_paid_for_premises: The occupants had paid an actual rent for the premises.
predicates.no_basis_to_disturb_rent_based_award: The evidence did not provide a basis to disturb an award tied to the actual rent.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges mesne profits and the evidence provides no basis to disturb an award based on actual rent, the award is limited to that rent.
